Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

so that conjunction

in order that: purpose

also in order to, so as to, in order that, lest, so that … not, to (in order to)

classical

Ov. Ars 2.107: ut amēris, amābilis estō
Quint. 6.1.46: date puerō pānem, nē plōret

ut, nē (+ subjunctive)

conjunctions, with the present subjunctive after a present or future main verb, the imperfect after a past one

so that, in order to; so that … not

English “to …” of purpose is a clause in Latin, never a bare infinitive: vēnī ut tē vidērem. A purpose to be avoided takes nē, not ut nōn; “and so that … not” is nēve.

Other words

  • quō (+ comparative and subjunctive) — so that (the more …)

    conjunction, where the clause has a comparative · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.97: respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem

  • supīnum (dormītum īre) — to (after verbs of going)

    the supine in -um after a verb of motion · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.5.48: lūsum it Maecēnās, dormītum ego Vergiliusque

    “Go and sleep”, “come to eat”: dormītum īre, cēnātum venīre. The gerund with ad or causā does the same work: see purpose.

Examples

  • ut amēris, amābilis estō

    to be loved, be lovableOv. Ars 2.107

  • Eāmus intrō, ut prandeāmus.

    Let’s go in and have lunch.Plaut. Men. 387

  • date puerō pānem, nē plōret

    give the boy some bread, so that he doesn’t cryQuint. 6.1.46

  • Nē cadam, amābō, tenē mē.

    Hold me, please, so I don’t fall.Plaut. Cas. 634c

  • Sōcratēn ferunt … respondisse sē, quō melius cēnāret, obsōnāre ambulandō famem

    they say Socrates answered that he was buying in hunger by walking, so as to dine betterCic. Tusc. 5.97

  • lūsum it Maecēnās, dormītum ego Vergiliusque

    Maecenas goes off to play, Virgil and I to sleepHor. S. 1.5.48

See also purpose, so … that, and not.
